newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW-CU plans Czech Republic operation.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-CU plans Czech Republic operation.

text.p: British-based composite insurer Commercial Union said on Wednesday it is hopeful of setting up a life operation in the Czech Republic early next year.
Finance director Peter Foster told Reuters in an interview the group applied several weeks ago to the Czech Republic's finance ministry for permission to set up a life business.
If the company is granted approval shortly, then it may establish the operation sometime during the early part of 1997.
The amount invested initially would be small, said Foster, but the potential for rapid growth is significant. Nearby Poland is the group's fastest growing territory.
"We would hope really to build on the success that we have seen in Poland and also build on the lessons that we have employed there," said Foster.
CU on Wednesday reported a slide in nine month operating profits to 348 million stg from 384 million and blamed increased weather losses in the U.S. and Britain earlier this year.
But strong profit growth from France and the Netherlands helped offset the 62 million stg increase in weather claims.
The group announced its results the day after French insurers Axa and UAP unveiled plans to merge creating a world insurance giant.

Despite the present fierce competition in the global insurance market and a recent decline in rates, which have put pressure on insurers to increase efficiency, Foster said CU was not inclined to seek economies of scale through such a merger.

"Size for size's own sake we don't regard as desirable. If you're an efficient company with reasonable scale, one can actually be pretty efficient and we continue to have one of the best ratios as far as the UK is concerned," said Foster.

"There aren't very many opportunities that arise where one can see the quality of the business for the right price being available. We keep our eyes open, but organic growth is something we feel we've been quite successful at in the past."

In Britain, much of the attention paid to the industry has been focused on the direction of prices, and personal motor insurance rates in particular, which have been in decline but which some insurers say now appear to be bottoming out.

Foster said CU has not made any rating increases, but did not reduce rates by as much as other insurers did when prices were falling. However, he added that the next move from CU on rates would probably be in an upward direction.
